independence.note: Semantic inputs were only own clean state, sanitized root/own role config, and public sources. Control/config were frozen before the first substantive semantic read.

checked_sources.source: Samuel Girard et al., Fast Best-in-Class Regret for Contextual Bandits, UAI 2026 / Online Policy Learning via a Self-Normalized Maximal Inequality
checked_sources.result: Direct recent evidence that a policy can be updated every round from adaptively collected data without pretending the learned policy was fixed in advance. The method minimizes a pessimistic clipped inverse-propensity objective with a variance penalty. Its sequential self-normalized maximal inequality is uniform over the policy class and variance-adaptive under adaptive data collection, yielding fast best-in-class regret rates, including polylogarithmic rates in the parametric regime under the paper's entropy and Holderian error-bound assumptions. This resolves part of the prior same-stream selection frontier: data-dependent policy learning is possible when the inference/learning guarantee is uniform over the controlled policy class. It is not by itself an anytime deployment certificate relative to a changing baseline.

checked_sources.source: J. Jon Ryu et al., Improved Offline Contextual Bandits with Second-Order Bounds: Betting and Freezing, COLT 2025
checked_sources.result: Primary source supports off-policy selection and learning from the same fixed logged dataset using variance-adaptive betting bounds and a low-variance 'freezing' learning objective that improves small-sample behavior. It supports the broader idea that candidate generation need not be separated from evaluation if a uniform policy-learning bound controls the data dependence, but its setting is offline data from a fixed behavior policy rather than an always-on adaptive deployment loop.

checked_sources.source: Ming Yin et al., Near-Optimal Provable Uniform Convergence in Offline Policy Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning, AISTATS 2021
checked_sources.result: Primary theoretical bridge: fixed-policy OPE bounds do not justify offline policy learning because the selected policy is data-dependent; simultaneous evaluation over an entire policy class does. This supplies the weakest clean statistical principle for same-data candidate search and evaluation: make the guarantee uniform over the class, not merely pointwise for a candidate chosen after looking at the data.

checked_sources.source: Ian Waudby-Smith et al., Anytime-valid off-policy inference for contextual bandits
checked_sources.result: Time-uniform off-policy confidence sequences remain valid under arbitrary stopping, adaptive logging policies, dependent/drifting contexts, and include time-varying off-policy reward functionals. This remains the appropriate optional-stopping layer once a candidate or predictable candidate sequence is defined, but it does not automatically make arbitrary same-stream candidate search selection-valid.

checked_sources.source: Pedram Rabiee and Amirsaeid Safari, Safe Exploration in Reinforcement Learning: Training Backup Control Barrier Functions with Zero Training-Time Safety Violations, L4DC 2025
checked_sources.result: Primary evidence for an orthogonal pathwise safety layer. Backup control barrier functions construct a control-forward-invariant subset and the reported inverted-pendulum training has zero safety violations while RL is used to enlarge the safe exploration region. This is much closer to hard trajectory-level safety than expected-cost constraints, though it relies on control-system structure and does not itself provide a current-policy utility floor.

checked_sources.source: Kyungmin Kim et al., Realizable Continuous-Space Shields for Safe Reinforcement Learning, L4DC 2025
checked_sources.result: Primary shield result proving realizability for stateful continuous-space shields, including non-Markovian safety requirements such as loop avoidance, while empirically preserving policy success rate on navigation and multi-agent particle tasks. This supports separating hard admissibility from utility optimization instead of scalarizing them together.

checked_sources.source: Adam Haroon et al., Learning When to Act: Communication-Efficient Reinforcement Learning via Run-Time Assurance, arXiv:2605.12561
checked_sources.result: Recent quantitative pathwise-safety evidence: a pointwise Lyapunov run-time-assurance layer overrides unsafe learned actions using a certified backup. On inverted pendulum, cart-pole, and planar quadrotor, the learned controller achieves 1.91x, 1.45x, and 3.51x higher mean inter-sample interval than a Lyapunov-triggered baseline while the safety layer remains active; removing the shield degrades the reported tradeoff. This is source-domain evidence, not a direct theorem for research automation.

checked_sources.source: Samir Khan et al., Off-policy Evaluation Beyond Overlap: Sharp Partial Identification Under Smoothness, ICML 2024; Philip Amortila et al., A Unifying View of Coverage in Linear Off-Policy Evaluation, 2026
checked_sources.result: Coverage failure should change the output type, not merely widen a point estimate indefinitely. Without overlap, valid OPE generally needs additional assumptions; under Lipschitz smoothness one can return sharp partial-identification bounds. The 2026 linear-OPE analysis makes error explicitly depend on a feature-dynamics coverage parameter. Operationally, insufficient coverage should trigger partial-identification/abstention or new data collection instead of a high-variance pass/fail certificate.

candidates_new.mechanism: Replace pointwise post-selection testing with a uniform-over-policy-class pessimistic bound when candidates are learned from the same evidence stream. The optimizer may adaptively choose a candidate inside a predeclared/complexity-controlled policy or configuration class because the statistical guarantee holds simultaneously over that class. For deployment at arbitrary times, add a time-uniform baseline-comparison layer or freeze the selected candidate into a fresh evaluation lineage. Never apply a fixed-candidate confidence interval to a candidate selected by maximizing that same interval over data.
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: Girard et al. establish fast best-in-class regret, including polylogarithmic parametric rates under their stated complexity/margin assumptions, while updating policy every round from adaptive data. The exact deployment-gate composition is not a single published theorem.
candidates_new.scope: Contextual-bandit/offline-RL style policy classes with appropriate importance-weight support, bounded rewards/controlled complexity, and the source-specific entropy, margin, or coverage assumptions. Uniformity is over the declared class; arbitrary class expansion after inspecting the same evidence is not free.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Class complexity can make uniform bounds too wide; overlap/coverage failure can make importance-weight evidence unusable; changing the candidate class based on the same evidence can reintroduce selection bias unless the class expansion itself is covered by a uniform/PAC-Bayes/online-learning guarantee or a new data lineage; regret guarantees are not equivalent to per-update safe deployment.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: For automation optimization, define a bounded configuration family before each evaluation epoch and use a uniform pessimistic score to search within it. Release only through a separate anytime current-baseline certificate or a fresh post-selection stream. This can reduce the need for repeated holdout splitting while retaining a clear statistical boundary.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the source-domain uniform-data-dependent learning principle; medium for the composed automation gate

candidates_new.mechanism: Use two non-compensating layers: a pathwise admissibility shield/invariant that can override or reject an unsafe action/config transition, and a separate statistical utility certificate relative to the current deployed baseline. The hard shield is checked first and cannot be paid down by later reward; only shield-admissible candidates enter the utility gate.
primary_sources: prior current-baseline/off-policy-CS sources in own state
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: RLBUS reports zero training-time safety violations in its inverted-pendulum demonstration while enlarging the safe exploration region. Haroon et al. report 1.91x/1.45x/3.51x higher mean inter-sample intervals than a Lyapunov-triggered baseline on three control systems under an RTA safety layer. These numbers validate source-domain feasibility of decoupled safety and performance, not the automation transfer itself.
candidates_new.scope: Control systems where a realizable shield, barrier, Lyapunov invariant, or trusted backup can be specified. Automation analog requires a machine-checkable invariant/rollback boundary, not a vague risk score.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: A learned or approximate shield is only as sound as its model/certificate assumptions; if no safe action is realizable, a shield can deadlock or require active information gathering; utility certification remains necessary because safe actions can be useless or overly conservative.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Map contamination/scope/CAS/single-writer invariants to a machine-checkable pre-action shield, while throughput/quality remains a separate current-baseline statistical gate. Do not let aggregate reward compensate for an invariant violation.
candidates_new.confidence: high for source-domain separation; medium for automation transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Treat support/coverage as a gate on whether comparative evidence is even identifiable. Before off-policy candidate comparison, compute a coverage diagnostic tied to the estimator's theory. If support is adequate, run the normal certificate; if weak but an explicit structural assumption is justified, return a partial-identification interval; if neither holds, abstain and collect targeted evidence instead of emitting an unstable point estimate.
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: The sources provide finite-sample/minimax theory and valid partial-identification bounds rather than a universal numeric threshold. The correct trigger is estimator- and representation-specific, not a fixed ESS constant.
candidates_new.scope: Off-policy evaluation and analogous counterfactual comparisons where candidate behavior reaches regions weakly represented by the logging/evidence distribution.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Smoothness/model assumptions used to bridge no-overlap regions can be wrong; generic ESS thresholds do not diagnose which decision regions are unsupported; forcing a pass/fail decision under nonidentification can create false confidence.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: An optimizer should be allowed to say 'insufficient comparative evidence' and allocate a targeted experiment when a candidate differs from baseline exactly where evidence coverage is poor, rather than optimizing a noisy surrogate score.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the abstention/partial-identification principle; medium-high for transfer

evidence_updates.update: The fixed-class limitation is not a universal blocker to same-stream learning. Girard et al. 2026 provide uniform sequential empirical-process control for policies updated every round from adaptive data, and older uniform-OPE work explicitly handles data-dependent policy selection by evaluating the whole class. What remains unresolved is a single finite-sample theorem that simultaneously gives same-stream adaptive class learning, arbitrary stopping, multiple independent utility/safety outcomes, and current-baseline deployment safety.

Pathwise safety now has a concrete orthogonal source-domain primitive: control-forward-invariant / realizable shields can enforce trajectory-level admissibility independently of expected utility. This removes the need to ask an expected-cost certificate to double as hard safety, but the exact utility-floor plus shield composition remains a synthesis.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A fresh holdout is always necessary whenever a candidate is data-dependent.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Too strong. Uniform convergence or uniform pessimistic bounds over a controlled policy class can support data-dependent selection from the same data. Fresh holdout remains a simple fallback when uniform class control is unavailable or the class itself was expanded adaptively from the evidence.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Use holdout splitting as a conservative fallback, not a universal requirement.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Sequential regret or pessimistic learning guarantees automatically imply safe deployment against the current baseline at every update.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established. Regret/excess-risk guarantees control cumulative or terminal performance, not necessarily a per-update high-confidence non-degradation condition.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Keep deployment certification separate from the learning objective.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A single effective-sample-size cutoff is a theoretically sufficient universal overlap diagnostic.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not supported. Coverage is representation/estimator/policy dependent; recent theory uses structural coverage parameters or partial-identification bounds when overlap fails.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Prefer theorem-linked coverage diagnostics and abstention/partial identification over one global ESS threshold.

frontier: Find a 2025-2026 theorem that is simultaneously time-uniform and uniform over a data-dependent or adaptively expanding policy/configuration class, not merely a fixed class or fixed-time uniform bound; inspect PAC-Bayes/e-process or sequential empirical-process constructions.

Search for multiple-outcome or vector-valued e-process/confidence-sequence methods that control familywise error under continuous monitoring with less conservatism than naive alpha splitting, and quantify the sample-efficiency price.

Quantify a practical coverage-refusal rule derived from a current OPE theorem (feature-dynamics coverage, self-normalized variance, or sharp partial-identification width) rather than a generic ESS heuristic.

Find a shield/invariant method whose certificate can itself be learned or expanded online while retaining a finite-sample failure probability, and measure the performance cost of shield intervention versus no shield.

Compare three candidate-evaluation architectures on a common synthetic sequential decision problem: frozen-batch + anytime CS, uniform-class pessimistic search + anytime release gate, and fresh search/test split. Measure wall-clock/sample use and false-release rate under adaptive stopping.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Followed the prior same-stream adaptive-selection frontier into 2025-2026 uniform sequential policy-learning work.

Resolved that data-dependent candidate selection can be statistically valid without a holdout when the guarantee is genuinely uniform over the controlled class, while keeping arbitrary class expansion as unresolved.
Added an orthogonal pathwise shield family so hard safety no longer depends on expected-cost certification.
Added coverage-triggered abstention/partial identification as a refusal mode for unsupported off-policy comparisons.

exact_next_action: Search recent PAC-Bayes/e-process and sequential empirical-process papers for a guarantee that is both time-uniform and uniform over a policy/configuration class whose effective candidate may be selected adaptively from the same stream, preferably with vector outcomes. If none exists, formalize the weakest safe composition: fixed complexity-controlled class + uniform pessimistic learner, separate anytime current-baseline release certificate, familywise vector certificate, pathwise shield, and theorem-linked coverage abstention; then quantify the extra sample/wall-clock cost versus fresh holdout splitting.
